title: BA1/1534/2020 of NEERAJ RANA ALIAS NIRANJAN RANA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
SL.
No Date
Office Notes, reports,

Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
BA1 No.1534 of 2020
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, Advocate for the
applicant.
Mrs. Meena Bisht, Brief Holder for the State
of Uttarakhand.
The present bail applicant is shown to be an
accused for commission of offence under Sections
363, 366-A, 376 (n) IPC and Section 5(1)/6 of the
POCSO Act, which was registered as Case Crime
No.63 of 2019 at P.S. Kotwali, Uttarkashi, District
Uttarkashi on 26.07.2019.
The prosecution story is that the complainant
on 26.07.2019, had registered a missing report
contending thereof that his niece i.e. the
prosecutrix, was found missing from the residence
and later on, the said missing report was converted
into an FIR, which was registered as Case Crime
No.63 of 2019for the commission of the aforesaid
offences.
During the course of investigation, the
finding which has been also recorded while
rejecting the bail application, though admittedly one
of the aspect which is quite apparently established,
is that the prosecutrix was shown to be a minor and
nothing contrary was brought on record to show
that she has attained majority on date of
commission of offence in view of the definition of
the child, provided under the POCSO Act. But this
Court for the purposes of present bail application
cannot be oblivious of the fact that if the statement
of the prosecutrix, which has been recorded under
Section 164 Cr.P.C. if that is taken into
consideration, which has been filed with the counter
affidavit. She admits certain vital facts, which are:-
(i) That she admittedly had eloped from
Uttarkashi, alongwith the present
applicant and reached Rishikesh by bus.

(ii) She admits the fact that on account of
threat exerted by the present applicant,
she stayed in Rishikesh in a Dharmshala,
where physical relationship was
established between the prosecutrix and
the present applicant.
(iii) She further admits that fact that thereafter
the applicant and the proseutrix had
travelled to Banglore by train and stayed
there for a certain period, where yet again
the physical relationship was established.
(iv) In the statement, which was recorded
under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. on
30.08.2019, she has submitted, that it was
Anil, the friend of Neeraj, who tried to
exert force upon her for the purposes of
commission of offence under Section 376
IPC, but somehow it was athwarted.
It was later on the applicant was arrested by
the police on 29.08.2019 and ever since then he is
languishing in jail.
The counsel for the applicant had argued that
in the medical examination report and the
supplementary medical report, which was supplied
by the Government Advocate dated 22.06.2021, do
not show the presence of any sperms, though the
medical report also records that no injuries has been
shown or found as such on the vital and private
parts of the body of the prosecutrix.
In support of his contention, the learned
counsel for the applicant has drawn the attention of
this Court to the statement of doctor, as well as the
medical report to show that there was a consent,
which was extended though a consent given by a
minor may not be relevant, but there was no
forceful commission of offence under Section 376
IPC as would be apparent from the medical reports.
Mrs. Meena Bisht, learned Government
Advocate had vehemently opposed the bail
application on the ground that since admittedly, the
prosecutrix was minor and it was not proved to the
contrary, that she has attained majority on the date
of commission of offence, still the applicant would
not be entitled for bail for the offences under

Section 5(1) to be read with Section 6 of the
POCSO Act.
Apparently this seems to be a logical
argument, because it is a physical age, which has to
be taken into consideration, not the mental age and
if the child is less than 18 years, in that eventuality
her statement might not be of much relevance, but
this Court also cannot be oblivious of the fact that
the child of about 17 years of age has categorically
made a statement that she has travelled from
Uttarkashi to Rishikesh by bus, stayed in a
dharamshala, then by train she has voluntarily
travelled to Banglore, without raising any alarm or
without lodging any complaint. Hence, the offence
under Section 376 IPC, might not be apparently
established against the applicant.
The investigation has been carried, Charge
Sheet No.73 of 2019 dated 25.10.2019, has already
been submitted and hence there is no possibility of
the applicant tempering of any evidence, the
Sessions Trial No.41 of 2019 is pending
consideration.
Looking to the overall set of circumstances
and particularly the medical report and the
statement of the prosecutrix, which was recorded
under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and also considering
the fact that the applicant is languishing in jail since
29.08.2019, this Court is inclined to grant bail to
the applicant subject to furnishing of his personal
bond and two sureties of like amount to the
satisfaction of the Magistrate concerned.
